drivingQuestion: Must the mishna, which has one recite Shema before sunrise, follow R' Eliezer alone?
outcomeNote: the proposal that the mishna must be R' Eliezer is deflected: it can be R' Yehoshua addressed to vatikin-style practice

segments.he: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, וְדִלְמָא כְּוָתִיקִין. דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וָתִיקִין הָיוּ גּוֹמְרִין אוֹתָהּ עִם הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה.
segments.en: The Gemara immediately rejects this assumption: «Even if you say» that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Yehoshua,» who disagrees with Rabbi Eliezer and holds that one may recite the morning Shema until the third hour of the day, «and perhaps» the halakha in the mishna was directed toward those whose practice was «in accordance with» the custom of the «vatikin,» pious individuals who were scrupulous in their performance of mitzvot, with regard to whom «Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The vatikin would conclude» the recitation of Shema «with sunrise.»

moves.cueHe: אפילו תימא רבי יהושע, ודלמא כותיקין
moves.summary: the mishna can even be R' Yehoshua: perhaps it was taught for those who practise like the vatikin
moves.about: the mishna need not follow R' Eliezer: even on R' Yehoshua's view it can be addressed to those who practise like the vatikin

moves.summary: R' Yochanan: the vatikin would finish Shema at sunrise — so a pre-sunrise Shema fits even R' Yehoshua
moves.about: the mishna was taught for those who follow the practice of the vatikin and finish Shema at sunrise
